title: IEEE 1800-2023 clause 34 (protected envelopes): what the two OSS simulators let a test observe

denominator.filter: clause starts with 34, checks and check_groups empty

envelope-structure.label_ja: envelope構造（対、入れ子、モード、字句スコープ）
envelope-structure.observable: Observable: acceptance of begin_protected/end_protected pairs, their nesting to eight levels, matching across an include boundary, and that unmatched delimiters are not diagnosed.
envelope-structure.unobservable: Not observable: replacement of an envelope by cleartext, encrypt/decrypt modes, pragma left-to-right state, re-encryption of a preexisting protected block, and self-containment, since no encryptor or decryptor exists.

encryption-encoding.observable: Observable: base64 is the only enctype Verilator accepts; the declared byte count controls how much text is discarded; line_length must be a multiple of 4; a data_block body is read from the line after the directive.
encryption-encoding.unobservable: Not observable: any cipher, IV handling, key or public-key selection, uuencode/quoted-printable/raw, per-field encodings, and any decryption.

key-block.label_ja: key block（key_block と key_* 選択子、data_decrypt_key の格納）
key-block.observable: Observable: the key_block directive starts a base64 body that Verilator consumes; a key_block and a data_block cannot both be carried in one envelope.
key-block.unobservable: Not observable: key selection, key wrapping and unwrapping, the digital envelope form and the uniqueness rules, because there is no key store.

directive-syntax.label_ja: directive構文（protectキーワードの字句と引数）
directive-syntax.observable: Observable: which spellings each parser tolerates (Verilator's lexer knows version, encrypt_agent, encrypt_agent_info, key_keyowner, key_keyname, key_method, data_method, encoding, data_block, key_block, begin_protected, end_protected and end; it rejects 20 of the 33 Table 34-1 keywords).
directive-syntax.unobservable: Not observable: any value a keyword carries, any default, and any effect, because neither tool keeps keyword state or produces/consumes a decrypted body; Icarus accepts every line as ignored text.

error.label_ja: エラー（規格が定める誤り条件）
error.observable: Observable: none of the specified errors is raised. The tools do reject some protect syntax, but for their own reasons (unknown keyword, base64 length), not for the conditions the clause defines.
error.unobservable: Not observable: unknown-key errors, illegal data_block/key_block input, nested encryption input, conflicting key_blocks, licence denial, because the conditions need an encryptor, a key store or a licence manager. The standard fixes no message or value for them either.

visibility-cleartext.label_ja: 可視性（data_block 外に平文で出る項目）
visibility-cleartext.observable: Observable: nothing. No encryptor runs, so no output envelope exists.
visibility-cleartext.unobservable: Not observable: which fields are emitted outside data_block (author, author_info, encrypt_agent, encrypt_agent_info, key names, comment, licence directives, viewport). Verilator rejects most of these keywords outright.

implementation-defined.label_ja: 実装定義（規格が実装に委ねる部分）
implementation-defined.unobservable: Not observable: extra cipher/digest/encoding identifiers, the licence library interface, and viewport access, which the clause leaves to the implementation and which neither tool implements.

digest.label_ja: digest（digest_* 選択子、digest_block、完全性照合）
digest.observable: Observable: nothing about integrity. Verilator rejects every digest_* keyword as unknown; Icarus ignores them.
digest.unobservable: Not observable: digest generation, digest encryption, placement and the comparison that detects modification, which need decrypted data and keys.

tests/ch34/test_34_extra_envelope_keywor.why: An empty begin_protected/end_protected pair is accepted as a directive pair and the declarations on either side elaborate; Verilator rejects `pragma protect begin_protected foo as unknown, so the bare spelling is what it recognizes.
tests/ch34/test_34_extra_envelope_keywor.limitation: No decryption happens: Icarus ignores the line, Verilator only records the delimiters, so the keyword's effect is not observed.

tests/ch34/test_34_extra_nested_envelope.why: Eight nested begin_protected/end_protected pairs are accepted by both tools and the design after them runs, which is the minimum nesting depth 34.2 requires.
tests/ch34/test_34_extra_nested_envelope.limitation: The pairs are empty. 34.2 speaks of encrypted data that contains nested envelopes; without a decryptor that content cannot be produced or recovered, so only the delimiter depth is observed.

tests/ch34/test_34_extra_include_envelop.why: Verilator opens an envelope in an included file (begin_protected, encoding, 24-byte data_block) and closes it with end_protected in the including file; its base64 counter and state cross the file boundary, and the module after the include runs.
tests/ch34/test_34_extra_include_envelop.limitation: Nothing is decrypted and the 24 bytes are arbitrary, so the test shows the lexical extent of the directive state, not recovery of protected text. Icarus cannot run it (it reads the payload as source).

tests/ch34/test_34_extra_data_block_skip.why: The data_block body is 32 base64 characters (encoding bytes=24) on the line after the directive, and Verilator consumes exactly those bytes and elaborates the module that follows, so the body was not read as source text (the bare 32-character token would be a syntax error).
tests/ch34/test_34_extra_data_block_skip.limitation: The bytes are arbitrary, not a ciphertext, and Verilator drops them instead of decrypting; only the placement and the exclusion from analysis are observed, not the encryption.

SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-ENCRYPTION-ENVELOPE.subject: Begin/end delimit encryption envelopes, with end associated with the most recent begin, subject to the explicit nonnesting rule.
SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-ENCRYPTION-ENVELOPE.reason: Neither tool checks that a begin/end encryption pair is closed: Icarus ignores the directives (P1) and Verilator accepts an unmatched end_protected and an unclosed begin_protected without a diagnostic (P12). A decryptor that paired the delimiters would be needed to observe the rule, and neither tool has one (P14).

SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-CONTENT-KEY.subject: Pragma expressions before begin/begin_protected are envelope keywords; those inside matching delimiters are content keywords processed within the transformed region.
SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-CONTENT-KEY.reason: Whether a pragma is an envelope keyword or a content keyword matters only to a tool that processes the envelope. Verilator rejects most of these keywords outright as unknown (P10) and keeps no envelope state beyond the base64 counter (P4); Icarus ignores them all (P1). The distinction the clause draws therefore has no observable consequence in either tool.

SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-TRANSFORMAT.subject: Protected text regions supply cryptographic/key/attribute/data information and are transformed before source-language analysis.
SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-TRANSFORMAT.reason: Both tools remove or keep the envelope text without decrypting: Icarus compiles the whole region as source (P3, P17), Verilator deletes only a data_block/key_block payload (P4, P15). There is no cleartext replacement, so macro expansion and recursive decryption of a replaced body cannot be observed.

SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-PROTECT-SEQUENCE.subject: Protect pragma expressions process left to right; splitting or combining the same sequence across directives must not alter envelope interpretation.
SV2023-34.2-EXTRACT-PROTECT-SEQUENCE.reason: Processing pragma expressions left to right is only visible in the state an encryptor or decryptor derives from them, or in output. Verilator keeps almost no such state and rejects most keywords (P10); Icarus ignores all of them (P1). Splitting or combining a sequence therefore yields no observable difference in either tool.

SV2023-34.3-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-MODES.subject: Encryption transforms source encryption envelopes to decryption envelopes; decryption replaces them with cleartext before compilation.
SV2023-34.3-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-MODES.reason: The rule relates source encryption envelopes to decryption envelopes. There is no encryptor in either tool (P0, P5: Verilator rejects `pragma protect begin; Icarus ignores it), so no source encryption envelope can be made and the replacement cannot be observed; Verilator only drops data_block bytes (P4).

SV2023-34.3-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-PROCESSING-.subject: Source-processing tools decrypt every envelope when supplied the proper key; encryptors need interpret only protect pragmas and apply no other interpretation to ordinary source text.
SV2023-34.3-EXTRACT-ENVELOPE-PROCESSING-.reason: Decrypting every envelope with the proper key needs a key store. Icarus has no protect option (P0) and Verilator's --protect-key does not affect IEEE envelopes (P14); Verilator merely skips the payload (P4). The decrypting half of the rule is unreachable, and the encryptor half needs an encryptor that neither tool has (P5).

SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-ENCRYPTION-REPLACE.subject: An encryptor replaces each encryption envelope with a decryption envelope encrypted according to its pragma expressions.
SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-ENCRYPTION-REPLACE.reason: The rule relates source encryption envelopes to decryption envelopes. There is no encryptor in either tool (P0, P5: Verilator rejects `pragma protect begin; Icarus ignores it), so no source encryption envelope can be made and the replacement cannot be observed; Verilator only drops data_block bytes (P4).

SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-EXCHANGE-KEY-DATA.subject: Specified envelope pragmas become output envelope/content pragmas and the body encrypted under the specified exchange key is emitted as data_block.
SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-EXCHANGE-KEY-DATA.reason: Emitting the body encrypted under an exchange key as data_block is encryptor output. Neither tool encrypts (P0, P5: Verilator rejects `pragma protect begin; Icarus ignores it), and Verilator only consumes an existing base64 block to discard it (P4, P6).

SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-OUTSIDE-ENCRYPTION.subject: Source outside encryption envelopes remains unchanged unless explicitly specified otherwise.
SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-OUTSIDE-ENCRYPTION.reason: Both tools do compile the text outside an envelope unchanged (P3, P17), but only because they leave the inside unchanged too: Icarus never recognises a protect construct (P1), and Verilator removes just the data_block/key_block bytes (P4). A test of the outside text would therefore pass for a tool with no protection at all and would not show that the rule was implemented, so it is not written.

SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-SESSION-KEY-OPTION.subject: An encryptor may generate an unspecified session key, encrypt it with the exchange key into key_block and encrypt the body with the session key into data_block.
SV2023-34.3.1-EXTRACT-SESSION-KEY-OPTION.reason: Generating a session key, encrypting it under the exchange key into key_block and encrypting the body under it is encryptor work. Neither tool encrypts (P0, P5), and Verilator cannot even carry a key_block and a data_block in one envelope: its single base64 byte counter runs out or overruns (P6).

SV2023-34.3.2-EXTRACT-DECRYPT-THEN-EXPAN.subject: Decrypting compilation replaces each envelope with cleartext data_block according to pragmas, then expands macros and recursively decrypts nested envelopes in the replacement.
SV2023-34.3.2-EXTRACT-DECRYPT-THEN-EXPAN.reason: Both tools remove or keep the envelope text without decrypting: Icarus compiles the whole region as source (P3, P17), Verilator deletes only a data_block/key_block payload (P4, P15). There is no cleartext replacement, so macro expansion and recursive decryption of a replaced body cannot be observed.

SV2023-34.4-EXTRACT-KEYWORD-AUTHOR.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects the directive line with "Unknown '`pragma protect' error" (P10), so the spelling and the value it carries are not read as this keyword at all; Icarus Verilog 13.0 ignores every `pragma protect line without a diagnostic (P1). No encryptor exists in either tool (P0, P5), so encryption input cannot be formed; Verilator's parser only consumes such a block as base64 to skip it (P4, P6) and Icarus reads it as ordinary source, so neither reaches the specified error.

SV2023-34.5.27.2-EXTRACT-KEY-BLOCK-OUTPU.subject: key_block content begins on the next line. For the stated signature mechanism form a text buffer from data_method, data_public_key, data_keyname, data_decrypt_key and digest_block as applicable, encrypt using appropriate key_public_key, encode with active encoding and output as key_block.
SV2023-34.5.27.2-EXTRACT-KEY-BLOCK-OUTPU.reason: No key store exists in either tool: Icarus has no protect or key option (P0) and Verilator's --protect-key is its own symbol protection, leaving IEEE envelopes skipped unchanged (P14). key_block bytes are never decoded, unwrapped or selected, and a key_block written next to a data_block in one envelope already fails Verilator's byte accounting (P6).

SV2023-34.5.27.2-EXTRACT-KEY-IV-PREFIX.subject: For key_method CBC requiring an IV, prepend the IV cipher block to encrypted key data before encoding.

SV2023-34.5.27.2-EXTRACT-MULTIPLE-KEY-BL.subject: Multiple key_blocks within one begin-end envelope must encode the same data decryption key data; changing data decryption pragma values between those blocks is an error. They provide alternative decryption keys.
SV2023-34.5.27.2-EXTRACT-MULTIPLE-KEY-BL.reason: The condition is an encryption-input error: several key_blocks in one envelope whose data-decryption values differ. Neither tool encrypts (P0, P5), so such input cannot be formed, and Verilator cannot carry a key_block and a data_block, let alone several key_blocks, in one envelope (P6). The standard fixes no message or value for the error.

SV2023-34.5.28.1-EXTRACT-KEYWORD-SYNTAX.subject:
The decrypt_license pragma uses the displayed keyword and argument grammar: decrypt_license = ( library = <string> , entry = <string> ,
              feature = <string> [, exit = <string>] [, match = <number> ] ). Parenthesized library/entry/feature strings are required for licenses; exit and numeric match are optional where bracketed.
SV2023-34.5.28.1-EXTRACT-KEYWORD-SYNTAX.reason: Verilator 5.052 rejects the directive line with "Unknown '`pragma protect' error" (P10), so the spelling and the value it carries are not read as this keyword at all; Icarus Verilog 13.0 ignores every `pragma protect line without a diagnostic (P1). No tool implements the keyword, so neither its grammar nor its effect can be observed.

SV2023-34.5.28.2-EXTRACT-LICENSE-DENIAL.subject: If decrypt_license authorization fails, perform no decryption and issue an error including the entry return value.
SV2023-34.5.28.2-EXTRACT-LICENSE-DENIAL.reason: Neither tool implements the licence interface: Verilator 5.052 rejects decrypt_license and runtime_license as unknown protect keywords (P10) and Icarus Verilog 13.0 ignores them (P1), so authorization cannot fail and the required error and the entry return value it must contain cannot be produced. The standard also fixes no message text or exit status, so even with a licence manager the observation would be tool-specific.

SV2023-34.5.28.2-EXTRACT-LICENSE-ENTRY.subject: After finding decrypt_license in an encrypted model, before processing decrypted text, load its specified library, call entry with feature string, and compare return value to match. Licensed return equals match; an unlicensed return differs.
SV2023-34.5.28.2-EXTRACT-LICENSE-ENTRY.reason: The entry/exit routines live in a licence-manager library whose interface the clause defines only for a tool that supports licensing. Neither tool reads decrypt_license or runtime_license (Verilator: unknown keyword, P10; Icarus: ignored, P1), and no library is loaded, so the call, its return value and the exit call cannot be observed.
